originality.rationale: Genuine distinguishing claim is exact affine conditional Gini mean-difference regression on one order statistic and hence globally optimal nonlinear one-coordinate predictor. The closest uniform-sample-variance order-statistic article already gives proportional rank dependence and identical asymptotic optimal rank fractions; these are expressly credited, not asserted novel. Its conditional variance regression is quadratic and cannot establish affine Gini projection. Closely relevant exponential Gini/order-statistic paper is different parent law. Two full 2014 Gini papers inspected without equivalent conditional formula. Residual risk: inaccessible full Hosking L-moment article or classical regression identity.
residual_risks: Classic L-statistic conditional expectation identities may already imply the exact affine projection: Hosking 1990 full text not inspected.
Same limiting optimal quantile and Pearson strength are already covered in a *different* uniform variance statistic; these are not standalone novelty claims.
One-quantile squared-error prediction under known uniform parent only; no multi-quantile or nonuniform extension.

value.rationale: Natural precise one-quantile compression question for a robust scale estimator. The exact same-sample affine conditional Gini regression is a structural property, ensuring even nonlinear transformations of a single ranked datum cannot improve squared-error prediction; exact R2, full finite rank/tie classification and 5/16 limit quantify a motivated predictive invariant. The shared variance-optimal rank percentages are credited and not used alone to establish value.
